newsitem.title: CUBA: No survivors found from Cuban air crash.
newsitem.headline: No survivors found from Cuban air crash.

text.p: Rescue boats and planes found no survivors on Saturday from a Cuban airliner that crashed into the sea near the eastern city of Santiago de Cuba with 44 people on board.
The Cubana de Aviacion Soviet-built An-24 plunged into the sea late on Friday shortly after taking off from Santiago on a flight to Havana.
Sources at the state airline said there were eight foreigners -- six Spaniards and two Brazilians -- on the twin-engined turbo-prop plane. They gave no further details.
Some 18 hours after the crash, airforce planes and coastguard cutters combing the site about 4 miles (6.5 km) off the coast had failed to pick up any survivors, they said.
A Spanish diplomat who flew to Santiago to assist families of victims told Spanish reporters that rescue workers had virtually ruled out finding any survivors.
The diplomat, consul Eduardo Cerro, said about 15 bodies had been recovered so far, including one Spaniard.

A civil aviation institute statement said there were 39 passengers on board and five crew members. It said the plane crashed into the sea minutes after take-off at 9:55 p.m. local time (0155 GMT on Saturday).
The statement said a state commission would investigate the causes of the accident. There were no immediate indications of what happened.

Santiago de Cuba, the island's second city, is about 530 miles (850 km) southeast of Havana. One of Cuba's oldest cities, it is a popular destination for foreign tourists interested in Cuba's culture and history.
The communist-ruled island's worst airline disaster occurred in September 1989, when 126 people were killed when a Cuban airlines plane crashed near Havana.
